resources.string: How it works

Google Maps can remember the places you go — that is your **Timeline**. This app opens your Timeline file, shows your trips on a map and saves them as GPX, KML, GeoJSON or CSV files for other apps (Strava, Garmin, Google Earth, Excel…).
This app does not track you and does not sign in to Google. It only reads the file you save from Google Maps, and everything stays on this device.
⚠️ Important — check this first
**Your location history comes from your Google account.** You need the Google Maps app, signed in with your Google account.
**Timeline must be turned on in Google Maps.** Google saves only the days since it was turned on — if it was off, there is nothing to export.
**Google Maps needs location access set to “Always”** (Settings app → Google Maps → Location), otherwise Timeline records very little.
**Timeline is kept on the phone that recorded it.** If your history was recorded on another phone, save the file on that phone.
Get your file in 3 steps
In **Google Maps** tap your profile picture → **Settings** → **Location & Privacy** → **Export Timeline data**.
Tap **Save to Files** and save the file to On My iPhone or iCloud Drive.
Come back here and tap **Choose Timeline file** below.
Detailed step-by-step guide
Try it with sample data
Made-up trips: see what the app does before exporting your own.

Google Maps keeps your Timeline only on your phone, not online, so no other app can read it directly. You save it once from Google Maps as a file, then open that file here. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
1. Turn on Timeline (skip if it is on)
Open Google Maps and tap your profile picture (top right)
Tap **Your Timeline**
Tap ⋯ (top right) → **Location & privacy settings**
Tap **Timeline is off** → **Turn on**
From then on Google saves where you go. Earlier days cannot be added later, so come back after a few days.
2. Save your Timeline as a file
Tap **Settings** → **Location & Privacy**
Tap **Export Timeline data**
Tap **Save to Files**, choose On My iPhone or iCloud Drive, then tap **Save**
3. Open the file here
Tap **Choose Timeline file** on the main screen and find the file. It is usually called location-history.json.
Or in the Files app: touch and hold the file → Share → **Timeline Exporter**.
If something does not work
**No “Export Timeline data”?** Check that you are signed in to Google Maps and that Timeline is on (step 1). The option appears once Timeline has saved something.
**Cannot find the menu?** Try: profile picture → **Your Timeline** → ⋯ → **Location & privacy settings** → **Export Timeline data**.
**Only a few days in the file?** Google keeps only what this phone recorded while Timeline was on. Also check that auto-delete is off (the cloud icon in Your Timeline).

**History on an Android phone?** Save it there: Settings → Location → Location services → Timeline → Export Timeline data. Send the file to this iPhone (Google Drive, email or a messenger) and save it to Files.
• On iPhone the file is called location-history.json, on Android Timeline.json. Both open here.
Choose Timeline file
This does not look like a Google Maps Timeline file. Choose the file you saved from Google Maps (usually location-history.json) — Help shows the steps.
iOS keeps each app\'s language in Settings.
